pr_title: Refactor BRP to allow for 3rd-party  transports
pr_body:
## Objective

Closes #15408 (somewhat)

## Solution

- Moved the existing HTTP transport to its own module with its own plugin (`RemoteHttpPlugin`) (disabled on WASM)
- Swapped out the `smol` crate for the smaller crates it re-exports to make it easier to keep out non-wasm code (HTTP transport needs `async-io` which can't build on WASM)
- Added a new public `BrpSender` resource holding the matching sender for the `BrpReceiver`' (formally `BrpMailbox`). This allows other crates to send `BrpMessage`'s to the "mailbox".

issue_context.title: JS Bindings for BRP
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

I'd like to be able to control the ECS of a Bevy app running in a browser from JS in the same browser window. My use case for this is an editor/inspector for my [Bevy Playground](https://learnbevy.com/playground).

## What solution would you like?

Currently the BRP only supports HTTP communication with JSON bodies. I propose that we extend this with JS bindings. This is because the HTTP communication relies on a server being hosted by the Bevy app which afaik cannot be done in the browser. The JS bindings would use the same structure as the JSON bodies in the HTTP communication. I do not believe this solution would require too much change/restructuring as it would just be a case of adding some extra bindings that use the existing BrpMailbox.

I do not believe fixing the [building on wasm](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/14880#issuecomment-2366767116) is in scope for this issue and propose we instead have some sort of conditional compilation/feature so only the JS bindings are included on WASM and not HTTP communication.

## Additional context

The BRP was recently merged in #14880.
JS Bindings were mentioned in the initial [BRP proposal](https://gist.github.com/coreh/1baf6f255d7e86e4be29874d00137d1d#possible-transports).

I'd like to have a go at implementing this and have put together this [playground](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2021&gist=f0e40c8ea877c7c0879e74dc2fcef2ca) on how I would do it.

review_comments: Can you explain the rationale for the change to `force_send`?
I think this ensures errors are reported even if the queue is full. This will overwrite regular messages to ensure the error message is always sent. Did I get that right @LiamGallagher737 ?

The previous `send_blocking` is not available on WASM. Another option is to use [`try_send`](https://docs.rs/async-channel/latest/async_channel/struct.Sender.html#method.try_send) but I don't think it is necessary as the channel is written to from in this function and only once. I could add some docs to support this.
